newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar trims gains as weakness returns.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar trims gains as weakness returns.

text.p: London white sugar futures trimmed some earlier strength on Wednesday as broker selling kept the spot March contract under the key $300 per tonne barrier, traders said.
Earlier in the session, market sources said trade covering of short positions had helped nearby values struggle back up from the lows seen after Tuesday's sharp sell-off.
"There's nothing doing, some premium selling capping it off and funds doing a bit of selling in New York," said one trader.
Sales of the March/May spread and the March premium were blamed for the market's failure to launch a sustained rally and buyers were said to be generally scarce, even at the low levels.
"I think London probably has some more room on the downside," the trader said.

The fierce bout of arbitrage selling on Tuesday pushed March to a $296.70 low and back to the upper limit of a downtrend channel in place since mid-September. But values then recovered slightly and March closed at $297.60, down $7.10 on the day.
At 1700 GMT March was down 10 cents at $297.50, just under its settlement price on Tuesday. It spent most of the day in positive territory.
May was down 20 cents at $297.90, maintaining the nearby contango, but overall volume was light at 982 lots.
Paris trading was very light at a total 281 lots. March and May were both up 10 cents and both at $297.60.
